+version: 2
+
+semantic_models:
+  - name: fct_signal_daily
+    description: 'One row per signal per UTC day inside the study and control windows, with its place relative to release. Population: Signal-days whose date falls in dim_date; days outside the spine are dropped by the inner join.'
+    model: ref('fct_signal_daily')
+    defaults:
+      agg_time_dimension: signal_date
+    entities:
+      - name: signal_day
+        type: primary
+        expr: signal_day_key
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+    dimensions:
+      - name: source
+        type: categorical
+        description: google_trends, bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: signal
+        type: categorical
+        description: What is counted, e.g. search:pto, posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: signal_family
+        type: categorical
+        description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: geo
+        type: categorical
+        description: US or WORLD. Only Google Trends has a US slice.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: signal_date
+        type: time
+        type_params:
+          time_granularity: day
+        description: UTC day (Google's own day for Trends).
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: study_year
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: days_from_release
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: days
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: iso_day_of_week
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: comparison_role
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: NULL except on the two compared Thursdays
+    measures:
+      - name: signal_value_measure
+        agg: sum
+        expr: signal_value
+        description: Daily value of a signal. Counts for posts and pageviews, 0-100 relative interest for Trends. Only meaningful grouped by source, signal and geo; never add across signals.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: count or index (see signal)
+              additivity: non_additive
+              null_rule: NULL when the value could not be read
+    config:
+      meta:
+        dex:
+          population:
+            rule: Signal-days whose date falls in dim_date; days outside the spine are dropped by the inner join.
+          assumptions:
+            - decision: Days outside the window
+              chosen: dropped
+              evidence: request
+              detail: the study compares Thursdays in Oct-Nov 2026 against the same weeks of 2025; the inner join to dim_date keeps only that spine
+              column: signal_date
+            - decision: Surrogate key
+              chosen: md5 of the natural grain
+              evidence: default
+              detail: the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity

+version: 2
+
+semantic_models:
+  - name: fct_thursday_lift
+    description: 'One row per signal per study year: the release Thursday''s value over the Thursday before. Population: Every (source, signal, geo, study year) that has a row on either compared Thursday.'
+    model: ref('fct_thursday_lift')
+    defaults:
+      agg_time_dimension: release_day
+    entities:
+      - name: thursday_lift
+        type: primary
+        expr: thursday_lift_key
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+    dimensions:
+      - name: source
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: signal
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: signal_family
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: geo
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: study_year
+        type: categorical
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: release_day
+        type: time
+        type_params:
+          time_granularity: day
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+      - name: is_index_component
+        type: categorical
+        description: True for the day-off intent signals of Google Trends (baseline >= 5), Bluesky and Reddit.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+    measures:
+      - name: baseline_value
+        agg: max
+        expr: baseline_value
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: count or index
+              null_rule: NULL when the baseline Thursday is not available
+              additivity: non_additive
+      - name: release_value
+        agg: max
+        expr: release_value
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: count or index
+              null_rule: NULL until the release Thursday has closed and loaded
+              additivity: non_additive
+      - name: lift
+        agg: max
+        expr: lift
+        description: release_value / baseline_value. 1.0 = a normal week.
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: ratio
+              null_rule: NULL unless both Thursdays are available and the baseline is above zero
+              additivity: non_additive
+    config:
+      meta:
+        dex:
+          population:
+            rule: Every (source, signal, geo, study year) that has a row on either compared Thursday.
+          assumptions:
+            - decision: Index components
+              chosen: day_off_intent signals of google_trends, bluesky and reddit
+              evidence: request
+              detail: Hacker News is too sparse (334 hits in 107 days, .dex/review/05); Wikipedia is hype or reference only
+            - decision: Low-resolution Trends terms
+              chosen: excluded from the index when the baseline is below 5
+              evidence: data
+              detail: Trends rounds to integers; a baseline of 1-4 turns a one-point wobble into a 25-100% lift
+            - decision: Surrogate key
+              chosen: md5 of the natural grain
+              evidence: default
+              detail: the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity

+version: 2
+
+semantic_models:
+  - name: fct_day_off_index
+    description: 'One row per study year: the Day-Off Index and each source''s lift. Population: Study years with at least one index component.'
+    model: ref('fct_day_off_index')
+    defaults:
+      agg_time_dimension: release_day
+    entities:
+      - name: index_year
+        type: primary
+        expr: study_year
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+    dimensions:
+      - name: study_year
+        type: categorical
+        expr: study_year
+        description: 2026 = GTA 6 release year; 2025 = seasonality control.
+      - name: release_day
+        type: time
+        type_params:
+          time_granularity: day
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              null_rule: never
+    measures:
+      - name: day_off_index_measure
+        agg: max
+        expr: day_off_index
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: index (100 = normal week)
+              null_rule: NULL until every component source has a lift
+              additivity: non_additive
+      - name: google_trends_lift
+        agg: max
+        expr: google_trends_lift
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: ratio
+              additivity: non_additive
+      - name: bluesky_lift
+        agg: max
+        expr: bluesky_lift
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: ratio
+              additivity: non_additive
+      - name: reddit_lift
+        agg: max
+        expr: reddit_lift
+        config:
+          meta:
+            dex:
+              unit: ratio
+              additivity: non_additive
+    config:
+      meta:
+        dex:
+          population:
+            rule: Study years with at least one index component.
+          assumptions:
+            - decision: How lifts combine
+              chosen: geometric mean within each source, then across sources, equal weights
+              evidence: default
+              detail: lifts are ratios; the geometric mean keeps one noisy source from dominating
+            - decision: A zero lift
+              chosen: floored at 0.01 before the log
+              evidence: default
+              detail: ln(0) is undefined; a component that fell to zero still pulls the index down hard
+            - decision: Incomplete index
+              chosen: NULL until every component source has a lift
+              evidence: request
+              detail: missing is unavailable, never zero

+version: 2
+
+metrics:
+  - name: day_off_index
+    label: Day-Off Index
+    description: Geometric mean of the Thursday lifts of the day-off intent signals (Google Trends, Bluesky, Reddit), x 100. 100 is a normal week. Group by index_year__study_year.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: day_off_index_measure
+
+  - name: day_off_index_2026
+    label: Day-Off Index, GTA week (2026)
+    description: The Day-Off Index for release Thursday 19 Nov 2026 against Thursday 12 Nov 2026.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: day_off_index_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('index_year__study_year') }} = 2026
+
+  - name: day_off_index_2025
+    label: Day-Off Index, control week (2025)
+    description: The same index for Thu 20 Nov 2025 against Thu 13 Nov 2025, before GTA 6. The seasonal baseline.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: day_off_index_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('index_year__study_year') }} = 2025
+
+  - name: day_off_index_gta_effect
+    label: Day-Off Index, net of season
+    description: The 2026 index divided by the 2025 control index, x 100. What is left after the pre-Thanksgiving drift. 100 = GTA 6 changed nothing.
+    type: derived
+    type_params:
+      expr: 100 * day_off_index_2026 / nullif(day_off_index_2025, 0)
+      metrics:
+        - name: day_off_index_2026
+        - name: day_off_index_2025
+
+  - name: thursday_lift
+    label: Thursday lift
+    description: Release Thursday's value over the Thursday before, per signal. 1.0 = a normal week. Group by thursday_lift__source, __signal, __geo and __study_year.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: lift
+
+  - name: signal_value
+    label: Signal value
+    description: Daily value of a signal. Always group by signal_day__source, signal_day__signal and signal_day__geo; never add across signals.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: signal_value_measure
+
+  - name: signal_value_prior_week_ratio
+    label: Signal, week over week
+    description: A signal's value over its value seven days earlier. On a Thursday this is the Thursday lift.
+    type: derived
+    type_params:
+      expr: signal_value / nullif(signal_value_prior_week, 0)
+      metrics:
+        - name: signal_value
+        - name: signal_value
+          offset_window: 1 week
+          alias: signal_value_prior_week
+
+  - name: day_off_mentions
+    label: Day-off mentions
+    description: Posts saying someone is taking time off (any reason), summed over seed phrases. Group by signal_day__source.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: signal_value_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('signal_day__signal') }} = 'posts:day_off'
+
+  - name: day_off_mentions_gta
+    label: Day-off mentions that say GTA
+    description: Posts saying someone is taking time off that also mention GTA.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: signal_value_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('signal_day__signal') }} = 'posts:day_off_gta'
+
+  - name: gta_share_of_day_off_talk
+    label: GTA share of day-off talk
+    description: Day-off posts that mention GTA, as a share of all day-off posts. A fraction (0 to 1). Thursday-is-chattier effects cancel out.
+    type: ratio
+    type_params:
+      numerator: day_off_mentions_gta
+      denominator: day_off_mentions
+
+  - name: gta_wiki_pageviews
+    label: GTA VI Wikipedia pageviews
+    description: Daily user pageviews of the English Wikipedia article Grand Theft Auto VI. The hype line.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: signal_value_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('signal_day__signal') }} = 'pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi'
+
+  - name: search_interest
+    label: Search interest
+    description: Google Trends relative interest (0-100 within one request). Group by signal_day__signal and signal_day__geo.
+    type: simple
+    type_params:
+      measure: signal_value_measure
+    filter: |
+      {{ Dimension('signal_day__source') }} = 'google_trends'
